C-FOLD-MEMBERSHIP-RECOVERY-1-DE8479F1.IntentSummary:
**This T2 plan converts the approved `C-FOLD-MEMBERSHIP-RECOVERY-1-DE8479F1` spec into four sequential implementation tasks plus one close-ratchet task. It is B2 of the maintainer-directed split of the monolithic `C-SUPERSEDE-MEMBERSHIP-2-C459A20C`; B1 is closed and committed, B3 (`C-SUPERSEDE-INTEGRATION-CLOSE`) remains reserved, and this bundle is independently implementable and verifiable with B1/B3-only behavior unchanged.** Durable modules are exactly `M-CURSOR` and `M-ARTIFACT-TYPES`; their verification anchors are `V-M-CURSOR` and `V-M-ARTIFACT-TYPES`.
**T-001 — disappearing membership tolerance:** `listLooseEvents` and `listRunOrphans` omit an entry that vanished between `readdirSync` and the read in both measured F295 windows, fabricating no filename-derived event and never letting an `ENOENT` escape, while `EISDIR` and every other read failure still propagate; the real `cursor show` / `status` / `gate archive` consumers keep their exact present and removed diagnostics. **T-002 — malformed loose input and fold consequences:** an existing-but-unparseable loose `run/` file stays visible to the read-only inventory (filename fallback, `cursor show` exit 0) and outside loose-file lint, but the fold boundary refuses it before any `discarded`/auto-open/ledger write; the three fold-consequence rows (interior hole refuses, trailing disappearance folds the survivors, vanished `opened` synthesizes only the legitimate covering `opened`) are driven through the real CLI. **T-003 — interrupted and mixed fold recovery:** the loose set is compared to the durable ledger before loose-only checks or auto-open, so an interrupted or partially deleted fold resumes against its recorded epoch without duplicating it, a genuine payload conflict or an older-epoch id reuse refuses without writes, and mixed residue plus a fresh set is ordered validate-first/destroy-last with the exact `F` / `F ∪ A` hook post-states and the post-ledger `C-RUN-LEDGER` boundary preserved. **T-004 — discarded preflight and F158 closure:** a preflight called by the fold/discard operation mirrors fold's allocation and single-controller auto-open semantics (including the `discarded` closer it is about to write) in memory and refuses the deterministic too-narrow-allocation, duplicate-id, pre-existing-hole, and no-allocation streams before the engine-authored `discarded` write, while the repaired positive control still writes exactly one `discarded`. **T-005 — close ratchets:** `src/artifact/scope.test.ts` is re-authored to this bundle's exact id and base with identity-bound lifecycle recognition (a planted non-lifecycle file inside the bundle directory reddens), and `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` gains the seven `bundleMinted` pins and the seven-token payer ratchet.
**Payment and record writes.** The plan grammar has no `<Pays>` element: the payment semantics live in this `IntentSummary` and in the spec, are carried structurally by the successor-named `registry.xml` charter row's `<Pays>` child (written by the close's `--flush`), are pinned by the seven `bundleMinted` entries in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (written by T-005), and are stamped as the derived `<PaidBy>` on the retired Finding carriers in `findings-retired.xml` (written by the close's `--retire` after this bundle's archive arrival). The payment is exactly `F292 F295 F292.1 F295.1 F313 F315 F158`. The staged handoff is exactly the **six** `Owner:` lines in `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` at `:79` (`F292`), `:121` (`F295`), `:143` (`F292.1`), `:158` (`F295.1`), `:184` (`F313`), and `:217` (`F315`); `F158` is already a durable live Finding and has **no** staged line, so the obsolete “seven staged substitutions” count is not carried. While this bundle is active, `--flush` writes the four live record XML files; an eligible `--retire` writes all seven XML files; neither writer writes `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md`, so this plan omits it. The exact non-lifecycle source, test, scratch, and record paths are enumerated in `ObservedWriteScope`; the close's writes are in the plan because the spec assigns them to the close, not to a task. This fresh bundle has **no predecessor supersede transition**.
**Baseline, gates, and close.** `9584bf913bf9760a2511fa0b99fe8684836dd117` is the spec's whole-bundle byte-invariance and scope-guard base. Every task runs its narrow instrument; the full CI-equivalent `bun run validate:ci` is the plan's single `TargetAssertions` `MustPassCommand` and the outer final gate, never a per-task command. The four spec `CloseEvidence` criteria (`AC-NO-UNFORCED-WRITES`, `AC-CLOSE-PAYER`, `AC-CLOSE-LINT`, `AC-CLOSE-TESTS`) are evaluated by the close in the applied-archive state and are deliberately absent from every task's `Satisfies`. The later plan's `ObservedWriteScope` must not add this bundle's own `spec.xml`, `plan.xml`, `design-context.xml`, `run/`, `run.xml`, or `run-ledger.xml`, because those are governed by identity/lifecycle rules.

T-001.Title: Disappearing loose-event membership tolerance and orphan consumers

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: In `src/artifact/run-membership.ts`, a `run/` event removed after `readdirSync` enumeration but before the callee existence check is omitted by `listLooseEvents` — no filename-derived fabricated entry — and a real `bun run ngrace cursor show` exits 0 with the surviving events and unchanged id order. The drive goes through the approved named test-only seam `setLooseEventReadProbeForTests` and the interceptor must report it fired. The same fixture driven against an isolated copy of base `9584bf913bf9760a2511fa0b99fe8684836dd117` observes the fabricated entry, whose discriminating shape is pinned exactly: `exists:false`, filename-derived `{id, task, kind}` attributes, and empty children.

An event removed after the callee existence check but before the read is omitted without an uncaught `ENOENT`: `bun run ngrace cursor show` exits 0, and a direct `listLooseEvents` call returns the survivors with unchanged payload and id order. The seam is driven to raise the late-window `ENOENT` and must report it fired. The isolated baseline copy exits 1 with the uncaught `ENOENT` through `src/artifact/xml.ts:219` and `src/artifact/run-membership.ts:70`.

`listRunOrphans` tolerates a well-named file that vanishes in the late window: a direct call does not throw `ENOENT`, and the two orphan classes (`event-filename`, `invalid-id`) keep their reasons and ordering. The real consuming CLI path keeps its exact diagnostics on a `C-ORPH` bundle whose `run/` holds `2-T-001-progress.xml` with `id="x"`: present — `status` exits 0 with `orphans=1` and `gate archive` exits 0 with `1 orphan(s): 2-T-001-progress.xml (invalid-id)`; removed before enumeration — both exit 0, `status` prints no `orphans=` for the change, and the gate prints `no-open-epoch … run/ empty`; removed after the existence check before the read — both exit 0. The late window is driven through the seam, which must report it fired before either consumer's exit 0 is accepted.

The tolerance is bounded to disappearance only: an event path replaced by a directory still exits non-zero naming the path (`EISDIR` preserved), and a `readGraceXmlArtifact` failure other than `ENOENT` and `xml.missing-file` still propagates. `src/artifact/xml.ts` is not widened.

T-002.Title: Unparseable loose input refused at the fold boundary and the three fold consequences

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `listLooseEvents` exposes the parse state of an existing-but-unparseable loose file (`xml.parse`, `root: null`) while keeping its filename-derived read-only inventory entry: a direct call still returns the entry with no root and no children, `bun run ngrace cursor show` exits 0, and `bun run ngrace lint --path <root> --fail-on errors` exits 0 with no loose-file issue on a structurally valid approved-spec/approved-plan fixture.

The authoritative fold boundary in `src/grace-cursor.ts` refuses an existing-but-unparseable loose file for **both** a malformed closer (`run/2-T-001-terminal.xml` = `<broken`) and a malformed progress event, before any `discarded` write, auto-open, or ledger write, naming the file and the parse error and preserving every input byte. Controls remain distinct: a valid XML closer folds (exit 0); a simply absent file is tolerated as the F295 disappearance; a parseable event with omitted attributes keeps the legacy filename fallback; a `run/` path replaced by a directory exits non-zero with `EISDIR`.

The three fold-consequence rows are driven through the real CLI, each with its own fixture and a recursive snapshot that records directory entries as well as file bytes: an interior hole refuses (`range hole at 2 for w0`) with the `run/` listing byte-identical and no ledger; a trailing progress materialized with bytes, then removed through the named seam after `readdirSync(run/)` and before the callee existence check, with `opened` and `terminal` remaining, folds with exit 0 and exactly the surviving events and no fabricated ghost; the drive asserts the after-enumeration interceptor fired; a vanished `opened` with `terminal` and `progress` remaining folds with exit 0 and a synthesized covering `opened` carrying a fresh covering id and no event for the vanished id. The criterion forbids treating every vanished entry as a refusal and forbids a ghost event.

T-003.Title: Interrupted and mixed fold recovery against the durable ledger

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: For each of `injectFailureBeforeVerify` and `injectFailureAfterWrite`, and for repeated interruptions at either hook, the throw leaves exactly one recorded epoch and the loose files; a real `bun run ngrace cursor fold` then exits 0 and leaves exactly one epoch containing each event exactly once, and a second interruption followed by a successful fold still leaves one epoch. A third, empty fold is the existing no-op: it returns the same epoch and `eventCount 0` and writes nothing. The fresh-only newly allocated control (ids matching no recorded event) folds normally into the next epoch, proving the recovery path does not refuse legitimate new events. A partial verified deletion (the first event of the verified set removed in the shipped delete-loop order) is resumed, not treated as conflict: the retry exits 0, reuses the interrupted epoch, adds no new epoch and no synthesized `opened`, and leaves no loose files. Payload preservation is asserted through `expectedLedgerEventAttributes` plus children, never the writer's transform.

A genuine payload conflict (a loose id matching a recorded event with a different canonical payload) refuses non-zero naming the id and mismatch, writes no new epoch, and leaves the recorded bytes byte-identical; a payload-matching subset of the last recorded epoch resumes; a loose id matching an event in an **older** recorded epoch refuses; untouched older epochs are never rewritten and no `opened` is synthesized for an already-recorded epoch.

Mixed recovery — matching residue plus a normally allocated fresh set **F** — is ordered validate first, destroy last. A pre-mutation validation refusal (e.g. a progress-only fresh set) writes nothing, materializes no auto-open, deletes nothing, and preserves every loose byte; `injectFailureAfterResidueDelete` leaves exactly **F**; `injectFailureAfterAutoOpen` leaves exactly **F ∪ A**; on success the matched residue is deleted, only the legitimate synthesized `opened` singleton is materialized when **F** requires it, the new epoch containing **F ∪ A** is written, and the fresh loose files are deleted. The normative state table holds across the interrupted states and the retry.

The post-ledger boundary is preserved, not relabelled F158: a fold interrupted after its ledger write may leave the written ledger and engine-authored loose events; the refuse path removes, renumbers, and rewrites no event or epoch it did not itself write, and a later fold recovers that evidence idempotently rather than accumulating it. No fold step emits an engine-authored `terminal`.

T-004.Title: Discarded preflight before the engine-authored discarded write and F158 closure

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A preflight called by the fold/discard operation in `src/grace-cursor.ts` mirrors fold's allocation and single-controller auto-open semantics in memory, **including the `discarded` closer it is about to write**, and refuses before any write when the prospective stream cannot fold. The exact too-narrow-allocation/unterminated-range row, the duplicate-event-id row (the F292.1 measurement), and the pre-existing-range-hole row each refuse with the **full `run/` set and its bytes unchanged — not merely “no file added”** — and a byte-identical `run-ledger.xml` when it exists.

The measured no-allocation stream `{1:progress, 3:progress}` refuses `range hole at 2 for w0` with no `*-discarded.xml`, no synthesized `opened`, and a byte-identical ledger. The repaired positive control (uniqueness, density, and allocation validity repaired) folds and the success path writes exactly one `discarded` event.

The bounded seam is retained, not serialized away: the preflight's guarantee is stated for the snapshot it reads; a controlled competing writer that changes the stream after the snapshot and before `foldEpoch` is recorded as a **stage-(ii-a) pre-ledger** outcome after `discarded` is written, explicitly not a stage-(i) preflight-snapshot outcome and not the distinct post-ledger `C-RUN-LEDGER` boundary; after that actor reverses only its own mutation, a real subsequent `bun run ngrace cursor fold` consumes the preserved `discarded` evidence exactly once, **creates no duplicate `discarded` evidence**, and leaves the final ledger/event projection correct. F158 names only the measured too-narrow-allocation/unterminated-range defect.
